as_told.title: Sculptor Michael Richards' plane sculptures and death in the Twin Towers
as_told.place_text: Miami; World Trade Center, New York

plain: The story goes that an artist working inside the World Trade Center made a piece showing planes flying into his own body, not long before planes hit the towers on September 11, 2001, and then died there that morning. Michels tells it in an episode with the scientist Rupert Sheldrake. He says the towers had an arts program, and that the artist showed himself as a Tuskegee Airman, one of the Black American pilots of the Second World War, with old fighter planes all flying into him, 12 days before 9/11. The writer Eric Wargo, who studies dreams and seeing the future and wrote a book called Time Loops, tells it in two episodes with more detail. He names the artist as Michael Richards and calls the work a sculpture, titled Tar Baby vs. St. Sebastian, rather than a painting. Wargo says the Lower Manhattan Cultural Council gave studio space in the towers to groups of 15 artists for six months at a time, and that Richards "alone among those artists" stayed in his studio the night of September 10th and was killed the next morning. They tell it as a possible case of an artist sensing his own future.
